title: Rambo: First Blood Part II
developer: Ocean Software (in-game credits: coding Tony, Dave, Bill and Martin; graphics Steve, Tony and Dave; music and sound Martin Galway)
build: Ocean's original disk, mastered 4 December 1985 ("MASTER DATE 04/12/85 NO:014.006.2" on track 18, sector 2), protected by the XROM system of Tequila Sunrise, Belgium; a G64 image

tools.emulator: release v3.13.2, v3.13.2-macos-arm64-gui.dmg (tools/vice-mcp), driven through kit/c64/vice.py and codemap.py; check-emulator 57 of 57 on release v3.14.0 (v3.14.0-macos-arm64-gui.dmg), which booted the disk the same way

exclude: runtime: zero page, the game's pointers, the object tables, the multiplexer's lists and the music driver's sequence pointers (named in the listing); game_init clears $03-$FF before play
not the game's: page 2 holds the loader's leftovers and a fill pattern, and no instruction of the game reads or writes it (references search, 2 November 2026)
not the game's: a regular fill pattern after the unused row drawer, which no instruction reads and the video chip cannot see (bank 1 is $4000-$7FFF)
not the game's: zeros after the unread glyph bytes
runtime: the jungle's screen and its sprite pointers, drawn from the map by the scroll code and the text printer; what it holds at the hand-over is overwritten before anything is shown
not the game's: a fill pattern between the arc tables and the music driver, which nothing reads
not the game's: a fill pattern after the tune data
not the game's: a fill pattern between the heroes table and the unreached sequence data
not the game's: the RAM under the colour RAM and the CIAs, which no instruction reads with the I/O switched out (swap_charset exchanges only $D000-$D7FF)
runtime: the working map, rewritten from the clean copy at $E770 by map_restore before every game and damaged by explosions in play; what it holds at the hand-over is never read
not the game's: filler between the clean map and the tiles
not the game's: a fill pattern between the last tile and the vectors

runtime: the music driver's voice state (instruments, return stacks, transposes, volume and the three voices' effect work areas), which tune_start, effect_start and the sequence commands fill before the driver reads them; named in the listing
include: authored: the jungle's character set, kept in the RAM under the I/O area at the hand-over and swapped to $7800 for play by swap_charset
